headline: Mammoth sign Artem Duda to two-year contract extension
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that the Utah Mammoth have signed Artem Duda to a two-year contract extension running through the 2028-29 season, framing it as faith in his rise.

The deal lands on a team that is playing well so far this season. UTA is 7-4-0 with 14 points through 11 games and controls 56.6% of the expected goals, a measure of shot quality that tells you who is creating the better chances. That edge is nearly as strong at five-on-five (58%), which suggests the results are built on sound play rather than special teams luck. The penalty kill allows just 0.53 expected goals per game, a good sign for a defender's role. The weak spot is in net: goals saved above expected, which compares what goalies stopped to what an average goalie would have, sits at -6.5. The skaters are doing their part, but the goaltending has given some of it back. Our data has no individual numbers on Duda, so the extension reads as a bet on a team that is winning the shot-quality battle, with the net as the open question.
